questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Relevant courses at my destination university.
- Exciting city offering many research opportunities in my field of study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Easy.
There was a lot, but my host university made it pretty straight forward.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Move-in details
Information about how to register my new address and sign up for the national health insurance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Three different dormitories for exchange student.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans, but every floor of my specific dorm had a kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Very convenient and a great way to meet other student from all over.
From what I heard the dormitories were a bit more expensive than other off-campus options.

Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a few difficulties with course selection, but these were fixed quickly and I was able to attend my planned courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online application form where you could apply for courses in three different rounds.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My department had an office where you could get in-person assistance immediately.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. I got in to all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of information and the application can be a little tricky so dont hesitate to contact your department office.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was lower than what I've gotten used to at UCPH and because there was a lot of homework you didn't really have time to pursue your own interests related to the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was more homework, class work, and student presentations than I'm used to. Not always beneficial and it meant you had less independence in your study.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

- Culture & Communication
- Race and Ethnicity
- Special Topic in Culture and Communication: State, Society, and Culture in the Middle East

questions.answer: In Japan it is manatory to sign up for the national health insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Supermarkets, restaurants, bars etc. were all much cheaper than expected.
Long-distance domestic travel was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many! Almost everything you could think of was available. It's important to note that many of these were not available for exchange students or people who don't speak Japanese.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't end up attending any of the clubs or social circle at my host university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city! almost every single area of Tokyo has something unique and exciting to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I got completely used to it after a couple of weeks.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are expectations that you act a certain way in public spaces that can seem detrimental to personal expression. This got pretty easy to navigate and adjust to though.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very detail-oriented, which shows in everything from food to music to architecture and much more.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- There's a lot of practical stuff you have to do when you first get to the school/city, so make sure you read all the documents that are sent to you thoroughly. It seems like a lot at first, but it is easier than you think.
- I really enjoyed staying at the dorms for exchange students. Met many great people who made my semester abroad even better than expected.
- Waseda offers many different courses. Some very specific. This makes it a great opportunity to explore interests that are related, but maybe not directly linked to your field study.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great people I met and getting to live in a city very different from Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
